title: OptimizeConfig
description:
Sequence alignment input shared by all commands that accept an alignment.

One flag name (`--alignment`, short `-a`, alias `--aln`) serves every command. `ancestral`,
`optimize`, `timetree`, and `prune` accept several files, one partition per file, numbered by its
position in the list (1, 2, ...); `homoplasy` reads exactly one file; `clock` does not read the
alignment. The path `-` reads uncompressed FASTA from standard input and may appear at most once.

alignment.description:
Aligned FASTA input, plain or compressed (`gz`, `bz2`, `xz`, `zst`); compression is detected
by extension. `ancestral`, `optimize`, `timetree`, and `prune` accept several files, one
partition per file, numbered by its position in the list (1, 2, ...). `homoplasy` reads exactly
one file. `clock` does not read the alignment. Use `-` to read uncompressed FASTA from standard
input; `-` may appear at most once.

tree_dialect.description:
Newick dialect of the tree inputs (the tree and the reference topology)

A dialect is a tree structure and an annotation convention, written as <structure>,<annotations>. The structure
is classic (plain labels and branch lengths), enewick (hybrid nodes such as x#H1) or rich (eNewick with support
and probability fields). The annotations are plain (comments are text), beast ([&key=value]), nhx
([&&NHX:key=value]) or mrbayes ([&B name value]). For example, enewick,beast reads networks with BEAST annotations
and classic,nhx reads NHX trees. TreeTime reads trees only, so a network input is an error.

alphabet.description:
Sequence alphabet

When omitted, the alphabet is auto-detected from sequence content and falls back to `nuc` when
detection is ambiguous.

model.description:
Substitution model to use

`--model infer` infers a model from the data. Alternatively, specify the model type. If the
specified model requires additional options, use `--model-params` to specify those.

model_params.description:
Parameters for the model selected by `--model`, given as a `key=value` list

Example: `--model k80 --model-params kappa=0.2 pis=0.25,0.25,0.25,0.25`.

partition_rates.description:
Relative substitution rates of the alignment files

With two or more `--alignment` files, all files share the branch lengths, and each file has
one relative rate that scales them for the sites of that file. `estimate` fits the rate of
each file with the rest of its substitution model fixed (a file with `--model infer` starts
from its fitted rate), then divides all rates by their mean weighted by the number of sites
of each file, so that this mean is 1. The branch lengths are then expected substitutions per
site, averaged over all sites of all files. `equal` fixes the rate of every file at 1.

With one alignment file, this setting has no effect: the run estimates no relative rate.

dense.description:
Use dense representation of sequences on the tree

Dense mode stores full probability vectors at every alignment position for each
node. Sparse mode stores only variable positions. Dense is more accurate when
branches are long and many sites change, but uses more memory.

output_all.description:
Write all default output files into this directory.

Produces the default set of tree and non-tree outputs for the command, using
`<dir>/<command>.<ext>` paths. Combine with `--output-selection` to restrict which
outputs are written.

Per-file flags (`--output-tree-nwk`, `--output-augur-node-data`, etc.) override or
supplement the files produced by `--output-all`.

An output that the run has no data for is skipped without a message, for example the
substitution model of a run that fits none. A per-file flag for such an output fails.

With several `--alignment` files, the outputs that carry sequence positions are written
once per file: reconstructed sequences, the augur node data of `ancestral`, Auspice, UShER
MAT, and Newick and Nexus trees in an annotated style. Files are numbered 1, 2, ... in the
order of the `--alignment` list. Their default names carry the number after the command
name (`<dir>/<command>.1.<ext>`), and the file name of a per-file flag for such an output
must contain `{partition}`, which is replaced by the number. Other tree outputs with
`{partition}` in their file name are also written once per file.

An output path that ends in `.gz`, `.bz2`, `.xz`, or `.zst` writes a compressed file. The
compression level is 2, unless the environment variable `GZ_COMPRESSION`, `BZ2_COMPRESSION`,
`XZ_COMPRESSION`, or `ZST_COMPRESSION` sets another level. `.gz`, `.xz`, and `.zst` compress
with all `--jobs` threads. `.bz2` compresses with one thread and is much slower to write and
to read than the other formats.

output_nwk_style.description:
NWK/Nexus annotation styles to write (comma-separated): `plain`, `beast`, `nhx`.

Applies to every NWK and Nexus output. With more than one style, files are distinguished by a
secondary extension (`.annotated` for beast, `.nhx` for nhx). Default: `plain`.

output_tree_nwk.description:
Path to output Newick tree file.

Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`. With
multiple `--output-nwk-style` values, a secondary extension is inserted per style.

With several `--alignment` files, the styles other than `plain` write one file per
alignment, and the file name must contain `{partition}`, which is replaced by the number
of the alignment (1, 2, ...).

Compression: path ending in `.gz`, `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zst` writes compressed output.
Use `-` to write uncompressed to stdout.

Parent directories are created if missing.

output_tree_nexus.description:

Compression: path ending in `.gz`, `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zst` writes compressed output.
Use `-` to write uncompressed to stdout.

Parent directories are created if missing.

divergence_units.description:
Units for divergence values in augur node data JSON output.

`mutations-per-site` (default): branch divergence as substitutions per site.
`mutations`: count of reconstructed substitutions per branch that change the state:
gaps, `N`, and ambiguity codes compatible with the parent state do not count.

output_augur_node_data.description:
Path to output augur-compatible node data JSON.

Contains per-node optimized branch lengths (divergence, substitutions per
site) and the input alignment and tree paths. The output is compatible with
augur export v2 --node-data.

Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

output_gtr.description:
Path to output GTR model JSON.

Takes precedence over paths configured with `--output-all` and `--output-selection`.

output_selection.description:
Comma-separated list of outputs to produce with `--output-all`.

Restricts which outputs `--output-all` writes. Special value `all` expands to every output
available for this command. Requires `--output-all`. Per-file flags are always honored
regardless of this selection.

A selected output that the run has no data for is skipped without a message, for example
the substitution model of a run that fits none. A per-file flag for such an output fails.

ladderize.description: Order tree topology before writing output files.

topology_order_target_file.description: File used by list or reference-topology target-order sources.

topology_order_target_aggregate.description: Aggregate used to map a subtree to a target-order position.

dp.description:
Likelihood convergence threshold. The loop stops when successive
likelihoods differ by less than this value, or when a 2-cycle with
amplitude below this value is detected.

branch_length_initial_guess.description:
Initial branch length estimate before the per-edge optimization.

- auto: estimate only edges with missing or invalid branch lengths,
  preserve valid input values (default)
- always: estimate all edges, overwriting input branch lengths
- never: use input branch lengths as-is; fails if any are missing

opt_method.description:
Per-edge optimizer. Both methods optimize in $\sqrt{t}$ space. Values are
`brent` (default) and `newton`.

no_indels.description:
Disable indel (insertion/deletion) contributions to branch-length
optimization.

When set, the optimizer uses substitution-only likelihood, matching
standard phylogenetic tools (RAxML, IQ-TREE, PhyML, BEAST) and
enabling v0 parity testing. Default: indels enabled.

reroot.description:
Reroot the tree by minimizing root-to-tip divergence variance.

By default, optimize keeps the input root. Pass --reroot or --reroot=min-dev
to enable divergence-based rerooting. Date-dependent methods (least-squares,
oldest, clock-filter) are available in the timetree and clock commands.

reroot_tips.description: Reroot on the branch leading to a tip or the MRCA of a comma-separated tip list.

keep_root.description:
Keep the input tree root instead of rerooting.

Optimize keeps the input root by default; this flag is the explicit form and
is mutually exclusive with the reroot options.

no_collapse_short_branches.description:
Disable collapsing of internal branches whose optimized length is zero.

By default the optimize loop contracts internal edges the per-edge optimizer drove to
exactly zero that carry no substitutions or indels, turning the resulting binary nodes into
polytomies. When set, such edges are kept in the output tree with length zero.

no_merge_siblings.description:
Disable merging of polytomy siblings that share substitutions.

By default, sibling branches in a polytomy that carry identical substitutions are grouped
under a new internal node. Requires the sparse sequence representation, so this step has no
effect under `--dense` and the flag is then a no-op.

no_flip_parent_child.description:
Disable the flip-parent-child step (reversion hoist) in polytomies.

By default, when a child branch carries the exact reversion of a substitution on the node's
parent branch, a new node is inserted that groups the node with that child, removing one
mutation per reverted position. When set, those reversions are left in place. Requires the
sparse sequence representation, so this step has no effect under `--dense` and the flag is
then a no-op.

gap_fill.description:
How to handle gap characters in input sequences

'only-terminal': replace leading and trailing gap characters with the ambiguous character (default, matches v0).
'all': replace all gap characters with the ambiguous character.
'none': leave all gap characters unchanged.

keep_overhangs.description: Do not fill terminal gaps (deprecated: use --gap-fill=none)

$schema.description: Path or URL of the JSON schema for this config; used by editors and ignored by the loader.

oneOf.description: Infer GTR parameters from data via Fitch parsimony substitution counts.
Estimate one relative rate per alignment file, normalized to a site-weighted mean of 1.
Fix the relative rate of every alignment file at 1.

InitialGuessMode.description:
Controls whether marginal reconstruction estimates initial branch lengths
from substitutions divided by effective alignment length. Preserving valid
input lengths can provide a better Newton starting point.

oneOf.description:
Estimate only edges with missing or invalid branch lengths, preserve
valid input values. No-op when all edges have finite branch lengths.
Estimate all edges, overwriting input branch lengths.

Use input branch lengths as-is. Fails if any edge has a missing or
invalid branch length.

BranchOptMethod.description:
Per-edge branch length optimization method.

Controls how the maximum-likelihood branch length of each edge is found:
Brent's method or Newton-Raphson, both in $\sqrt{t}$ space.

oneOf.description:
Brent's method in $\sqrt{t}$ space.

Derivative-free line search that combines parabolic interpolation with
golden-section steps. Optimizing $s=\sqrt{t}$ instead of $t$ smooths the
likelihood near short branches, so the interpolation fits better. v0
uses the same method and parameterization, with its own search bounds
and stopping rule, so branch lengths can differ from v0. This is the
default.

Newton-Raphson in $\sqrt{t}$ space.

Uses the first and second derivatives of the likelihood, including the
indel term, and converges in few iterations on well-behaved edges.
Choose it to compare against the default; branch lengths can differ
from the default and from v0.

OptimizeRerootMethod.description:
Reroot methods available in the optimize command.

Only date-free methods are valid here because optimize has no sampling dates.
Date-dependent methods (least-squares, oldest, clock-filter) are available
in the timetree and clock commands.
